items.title: Delhi High Court rejects NSUI plea over CBSE OSM row
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday refused to entertain a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition against alleged irregularities and technical failure in the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)'s On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for the class XII exams. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia disposed of the PIL filed by National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) without any orders after noting that a similar petition was recently rejected by the Supreme Court. The Court also observed that such grievances cannot be decided in a PIL. It added that the students can individually approach the Court or CBSE as per the prescribed framework. "We observe that claim for revaluation of answer book gives rise to individual cause of action to the student concerned for which it is always open for the student to take rederssal of the grievances with CBSE within framework," the Bench said. items.title: ‘Who gave the orders?’ BRS women MLAs allege police assault outside Telangana Assembly
items.summary: The monsoon session of the Telangana Assembly began with a serious confrontation between Congress and the opposition Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS). BRS MLAs wearing black clothes with anti-Congress slogans were prevented from entering the Assembly. Amid the scuffle with security personnel, BRS alleged that security personnel manhandled women legislators of the party. A video showed one of the security staff appearing to pull BRS MLA Sabitha Indra Reddy by her hair. Another woman MLA from BRS, Sunitha Lakshma Reddy, alleged that the police personnel pulled her saree. “As a woman who has been an MLA for decades, I have never seen such a situation. They pulled us by our throat, hair, and saree. Who gave the orders to do this? If the police behaved this way without the Chief Minister’s orders, actions must be taken against those responsible. Or else, the police acted on the CM’s orders, or to please the CM,” said Sabitha Indra Reddy, demanding an apology from Chief Minister Revanth Reddy. BRS MLAs began the day protesting against the Congress government’s alleged failure to fulfill its manifesto promises. items.title: What are the Sarkaria report and ED document Vijay cited to accuse the DMK of corruption?
items.summary: The Sarkaria Commission report of the 1970s is back in the spotlight in the DMK corruption debate in Tamil Nadu. For years, former Chief Minister and AIADMK supremo J Jayalalithaa had used the Commission’s findings to attack the DMK both in the Assembly and in her political speeches. Years later, the current Chief Minister, C Joseph Vijay, used the same report to launch a broad attack on the DMK, citing allegations of corruption during its previous tenures. The Sarkaria Commission was a one-man commission appointed in 1976 to investigate allegations of corruption and misuse of power against the DMK government that was in power in Tamil Nadu from 1971-1976. M Karunanidhi had been the Chief Minister then and many of the allegations that the Commission looked at were directly related to him. It was convened after Dravidian stalwart MG Ramachandran submitted complaints to the President, after he broke away from the DMK, alleging corruption involving Karunanidhi and his ministers. After the DMK government was dismissed on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency, Justice Ranjit Singh Sarkaria, a Supreme Court judge, was appointed to head the inquiry.
